newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge higher, seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge higher, seen firm.

text.p: Leading Russian shares nosed up in opening trade on Wednesday as world markets looked up and traders said prices would continue to rise throughout the day.
"The Dow Jones and European markets are looking better and investors feel much more comfortable buying," said Alexander Bubnovsky, head of sales at Alfa Capital.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index opened slightly higher at 289.12 after Tuesday's closing 288.63.
The market rose on Tuesday as leading shares followed a jump in national utility UES EESR.RTS after the government announced details of plans to tighten management at the company.
Traders said UES shares were still leading the pack.
"Without question. UES is the best mover at the moment," said chief equities trader at ING Barings Peter Kizenko.
UES traded at $0.2169 at 0800 GMT on Wednesday, up from Tuesday's closing $0.1995. Other leading shares were also higher.
Mosenergo MSNG.RTS rose to $1.22 from $1.17 and Surgutneftegaz SNGS.RTS was at $0.77 after $0.73.
Traders said Western investors' interest had been sparked by Tuesday's news about UES and would keep prices firm to the end of the day.
"We see some more orders coming from Western investors who were on the sidelines when world markets were in a difficult situation. I think today prices are going to be quite strong," said Bubnovsky.
